mechanism: Detect two break types on Bill Williams fractals: (1) simple — Close exceeds the last Up fractal High (or falls under last Down fractal Low), wait for bar close and enter next open; (2) complex — join last and last-but-one same-side fractals by a straight line, evaluate the line price at current time via analytic geometry LevelCalculate(Price1,Time1,Price2,Time2,NewTime)=(NewTime-Time1)*(Price2-Price1)/(Time2-Time1)+Price1, and flag penetration when Close crosses that interpolated level.
data_needed: iFractals upper/lower series; OHLC and Time[]; object or buffer storage of recent fractal prices/dates.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart symbol (NULL); current chart period (tf=0); fractal lookback up to MaxFractals; visible lines parameter.
why_new_for_mis: Separates flat horizontal fractal breaks from sloping two-fractal trendline breaks with an explicit time-interpolated price sensor, giving MIS a dual-mode structure-break detector rather than a single fractal arrow.
quote: A complex penetration uses 2 fractals – the last and the last but one. They are joint by a straight line that is expected to be penetrated by the close price.

mechanism: Argue that on short (intraday/weekly) windows price paths look like unrelated grow/fall/flat regimes and are dominated by unpredictable news spikes, while the same moves collapse to near-noise on a higher (weekly) chart; therefore sense market state and build systems on larger periods where news shocks do not rewrite the picture.
data_needed: Multi-timeframe OHLC of the same symbol for visual scale comparison; optional news-event awareness.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Unspecified FX charts; examples of one-week grow/fall/flat vs weekly chart; Championship news-spike chart.
why_new_for_mis: Frames timeframe choice as a regime-observability sensor: short TF = chaotic/news-dominated, long TF = stable structure—useful for MIS to gate short-horizon sensors as unreliable under news regimes.
quote: The use of technical analysis of short periods does not give a true and fair view, the market behavior is chaotic and unpredictable during short periods

mechanism: FractalsLine indicator latches the most recent iFractals MODE_UPPER and MODE_LOWER values into symbol+period global variables and draws them as persistent horizontal buffers; a close above the blue (upper) line or below the red (lower) line is a breakthrough. On rising markets trail SL under the red line; on falling markets keep SL above the blue line; opposite-line breakthrough liquidates. Explicitly useless in flat.
data_needed: iFractals(NULL,0,...); GlobalVariableSet/Get keyed by Symbol()+Period(); Close[]; optional iCustom FractalsLine for EA trailing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 (MACD Sample tests 2008.01.02–2008.06.30); chart symbol/period generally.
why_new_for_mis: Turns the latest fractal into a live horizontal break-level sensor and regime-conditioned trailing rule (trend vs flat), not just a one-shot fractal arrow.
quote: overpassing the fractal level often tends to continue the movement in the fractal's direction... Using this strategy at a flat market will produce no results.

mechanism: Over MaxLimit bars, for each price d from Low_min to High_max stepped by 0.0001, count how many bars satisfy Low[i]<d<High[i]; export (price, cross_count) to CSV/Excel; interpret local minima of the cross-count histogram as support/resistance because quotes cross those prices far less often.
data_needed: OHLC history (default 1000 bars); FileWrite CSV; Excel chart of Bars Num vs Cost.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart symbol/period; example levels compared to 9–10 Nov 2006 forecast (prices ~1.2582–1.2880).
why_new_for_mis: Senses barrier strength as inverse bar-occupancy density across price—an occupancy/touch histogram rather than swing pivots or order-book liquidity.
quote: the quotes will cross this line far less frequently than the other lines which are not support ones... count the number of intersections of the quotes and the price level.

mechanism: FindLevels indicator maintains CrossBarsNum[price] counts for a chosen TimePeriod; a price is marked S/R only if it is the unique local minimum of CrossBarsNum inside radius MaxR and the Max−Min span in that window exceeds MaxCrossesLevel; draws OBJ_HLINE with width/color/style scaled by timeframe; multiple instances overlay M15 thin dashed levels on M30 thick levels with alphabetical z-order so thinner shorter-TF lines paint on top.
data_needed: iLow/iHigh on TimePeriod; CrossBarsNum/CrossBarsMin arrays indexed by 0.0001 price bins; MaxLimit, MaxR, MaxCrossesLevel inputs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol; TimePeriod in {M1,M5,M15,M30,H1,H4,D1,W1,MN1}; example 30-minute thick + 15-minute thin overlay; MaxR ~0.0003–0.002, MaxCrossesLevel ~3–20 targeting 3–10 levels per TF.
why_new_for_mis: Adds significance filtering (MaxR + MaxCrossesLevel) and hierarchical multi-TF S/R overlay to the bar-cross density sensor, so MIS can stack short-TF vs long-TF barrier maps in one state.
quote: If a local minimum is not the minimum that belongs to the MaxR radius area, then it does not suit our task... If the maximum of function differs from the minimum less than by the MaxCrossesLevel in the MaxR area, we will not display this local minimum
